summary: Infogrames/Eden Studios' rally series, later revived by Kylotonn, known for console rally simulation, broad porting, and late-1990s WRC-inspired content.

entries.title: V-Rally
entries.definitive_edition: Windows Multiplayer Championship Edition plus N64 Edition '99 side route

emulation.emulator: Native PC / N64 emulator / DuckStation / handheld emulators
emulation.notes: Use Windows for main play; N64 emulation for the secondary Edition '99 route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC output with N64 secondary content

primary.why: The original V-Rally was ported widely after PlayStation. The Windows Multiplayer Championship Edition has sharper textures and online play, making it the best-fidelity main route. The Nintendo 64 Edition '99 has sourced updates, more tracks, and revised handling, so it is a secondary completeness route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows Multiplayer Championship Edition on a compatibility setup; sample the Nintendo 64 Edition '99 separately for its updated vehicle/track set.

secondary.exclusive_content: V-Rally: Edition '99 updates with revised physics, updated 1998 vehicles, and more than 50 tracks.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the N64 Edition '99 track/vehicle set after the Windows main route.
secondary.why: Windows has the higher-fidelity PC presentation, but the N64 version has sourced edition-specific updates.

entries.title: V-Rally 2

emulation.notes: Use PC as primary; Dreamcast emulation is a strong fallback.

primary.why: V-Rally 2 released on PlayStation, Dreamcast, and Windows. Windows has the highest output ceiling, while the Dreamcast and PlayStation releases are console alternatives. The planned Nintendo 64 version was canceled and is not a release.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release on a compatibility setup; use Dreamcast/Flycast as a strong console fallback.
